deities: Kamatchi Ammai / Kalyana Kamakshi (Sulini Raja Durga)

history.dynasty: Chola-era (inscriptions name the deity Rajarajesvaramudayar); later renovations incl. Tipu Sultan per one source
history.period: ~9th-12th century origins; Vaippu Sthalam sung by Nayanar Sundarar
history.summary: The 'Fort Temple' (kottai = fort) at Dharmapuri — ancient Thagadur, capital of the Athiyamans whose fort stood here. A Vaippu Sthalam hymned by Sundarar; inscriptions call the deity Rajarajesvaramudayar. Its maha mandapa holds two celebrated hanging pillars (~2.5 tonnes each) whose bases do not touch the floor, with carvings of damsels. The goddess shrine is described as carried by 18 elephants; Kamatchi is seen in full form only one day (Thakadur Kamatchi / Sulini Raja Durga) and only her face on other days. First worship is offered at the samadhi of Siddhalingesvarar. (VERIFY: '1200 years, built by Nolambars' is from a video description only; Tipu Sultan renovation from a single source; festival list is standard-only — temple-specific annual festival dates not sourced; coordinates from an online place listing.)

name: Kottai Kovil (Mallikarjuneswarar Temple)
town_description: Dharmapuri is an inland town and district headquarters in northwestern Tamil Nadu, the ancient Thagadur — capital of the Athiyaman chieftains of the Sangam age. It sits on the Salem-Bengaluru corridor (NH 44), with mango orchards and granite hills around it, and serves as the base for visiting the Kottai Kovil and nearby Adhiyaman-era sites.

travel.road: On NH 44 (Salem-Bengaluru highway); temple on the Dharmapuri bus stand-Tiruppatur road, next to the milk depot
